steps.content: You take several turns and stumble down a few flights of stairs. You couldn't have imagined the small motel having an underground space this huge.
As Mira drags you through the dark, winding passages, your thoughts race chaotically. You force yourself to stay calm and assess the situation.
Where are you taking me?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Ha... ha... Just know I'm trying to save you! If you had stayed there...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: We'll be safe once we're through this door! Hurry, I don't want anything to happen to you.
She makes a stop before a door, letting out a long breath. Her reassuring words now only provoke further suspicion and wariness from you.
You pull your hand free, your tone steely.
Thanks for saving me back there. But unless I'm mistaken... You and your motel are in cahoots with that smuggler, aren't you?
And it's not just you... The whole town of Tuco is in on it. This whole place is a Hypercube smuggling waypoint!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: No! That's not true!
Mira furrows her brow, her voice urgent but hushed as she protests.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: We would never stoop to colluding with smugglers! He... that man is just our prey... just like you.
Your expression turns grimmer. So everything here is indeed a trap.
Keep going. Since I'm your prey, are you trying to hog me for yourself?
Deep beneath the motel, the cellar is wrapped in complete silence, filled with only the musty scent of aged wood.
The girl lets out a sigh, averting her gaze before slowly beginning to speak.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You're partly right. Yes, the entire town of Tuco is in on it. The busy crowds you saw during the day were just an illusion we created in disguise. But we're no smugglers, we're just...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...putting on an act, working together to lure those smugglers and racketeers to get our survival necessities. Right, we're a bunch of criminals robbing criminals, says you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: And of course, sometimes, the loots include Hypercubes.
You recall the marks you saw on the banister in the hallway. You can't help but ask Mira the question.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: The smuggler? We've gotten rid of him, of course.
As she goes through the whole thing casually, new doubts surface in your mind.
If things are what you said, those people trying to catch me outside must be your accomplices. Then why save me? Wouldn't it be easier to just let them in?
Answer my first question. Are you trying to keep me for yourself? Or you set special traps for certain prey?
When you saved me, you used your special power. You... wanted me to know you're a Sinner, didn't you?
Your tone leaves no room for denial. Mira hesitates for a moment, then pulls a crumpled slip of paper from her pocket.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I thought you were another smuggler in the first place, going after the previous one's Hypercubes. I was going to follow the plan with everyone else and get rid of you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But while you were downstairs, I searched your room and found this. That's when I changed my mind.
You take the paper from Mira. It's a reimbursement invoice from some time ago, with an MBCC printed in the header and your signature at the bottom.
You must have stuffed it in your pocket a while ago and forgotten about it, and it just fell out in your room.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: So you're that MBCC's Chief, I guess? I've heard of that place... Some facility in DisCity whose mission is to detain and manage Sinners.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I'd like to... make a deal with you. I know you have the power to make it happen.
Mira takes a deep breath and looks up to meet your gaze, her eyes no longer avoiding yours.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I'll help you escape from here, and no one's gonna find out. In exchange, I need you to promise me one thing.
Mira's voice is firm and sincere as she makes her promise decisively, stepping forward to take your hand again. But you still can't trust her, instinctively taking half a step back.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Yeah, I know that.
She gives a disappointed smile and withdraws her hand.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But I really need your help. I swear I won't do anything to harm you.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Would you at least come with me? I'll show you I mean my promise. Whether you decide to help me or not... that's completely up to you then.
She reaches for your hand again, and this time you don't pull away.
Mira leads you forward through some passages, so mazy that you would never find your way out without her. After a while, a dimly lit basement finally appears before you.
She skillfully operates the mechanism to close the gate, then steps aside to press a switch on the wall.
After a noisy electrical buzz, pale light floods the basement.
As your eyes adjust to the brightness and the room comes into focus, you can't hold back a gasp.
What...?!
You're in a small, barely furnished basement. In the center of the room, a middle-aged man and a woman of similar age lie side by side, their lifeless faces as pale as the harsh light above.
Only the feeble beeps of worn-out medical equipment by their beds indicate they're still alive.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I know that I'm nothing more than a cunning con woman in your eyes... but please, just this once, you have to believe me.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: They need better treatment and medical equipment. You're my last hope. I can't lose them...

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Daddy, I found a mistake in the ledger! It should be 8, not 7 here. My calculation is correct!

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Let me see... Well, you're indeed right! So clever my lil lady, haha! Looks like I can hand over the motel to you and enjoy an early retirement!

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Dummy Daddy and Miracle Mira, haha!

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Oh my! Well then, would my genius lady like to guess what I got for her birthday?

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: ...Wow! A new dress! How pretty is this bow!

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: It is pretty, isn't it? And it's breathable, right? Or she will get heat rash if walking in the desert wearing this. Did you buy it with some secret savings, hon?

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: What... no, honey! The guest last night was a clothing merchant from DisCity. I simply gave her a half off for the rate. Didn't spend a single penny!

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Come on, dear, don't worry about money. Our motel's doing just fine. Mira's happiness is what matters most!
I've lived in this motel with my parents in Tuco since I was born.

It's really just a tiny motel. But for little me, it was just perfect. Its small door and windows kept all the bad things outside, while under our narrow roof, travelers from everywhere became my temporary family.
During the day, time always flew by at the motel in a flurry of activity. Mom would cook and clean the rooms, while Dad would greet guests and tend to their needs.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Buenas, traveler! My, that's quite some heavy luggage you've got there... Please, let me take those. Go rest in your room! No worries about a thing. As our guest, your only job is to relax and enjoy.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: ...Oh! Have you had lunch yet? I'm just cooking for my husband and daughter. Why don't you join us... No trouble at all, really! The pleasure is ours!
That's how they were, tending to every desert traveler going in and out of town with scrupulous care and heartfelt sincerity.
Dad always told me it's the host's job to make every guest feel at home. That's how I've run things since then, always keeping his words close to my heart.
At night, when three quarters of our world is covered by the starlit sky, we'd gather with our guests on the remaining quarter of desert sand, dancing and singing around the bonfire...

Our small town had its share of peculiar neighbors, but they were all good people. Some they'd also "play house" like we kids do, and when it was done, a party would be thrown in the town square. Though I didn't quite understand what they're doing, I always had fun then.
I loved our motel. I loved Mom and Dad, and my life with the townspeople then.
Then one day, the desert's starry sky began to lose its clarity.

The winds grew stronger, and sandstorms became more frequent. Armed raiders would storm into town, looting everything in sight. At the slightest hint of trouble, my parents would lock the motel's door, terrified.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Ugh... The desert bandits smashed our windows again. There wasn't much left in the storage anyway. Let them take what they want. But if this continues, soon we won't be able to survive in this town.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: We can't stay here any longer! Even if we could endure this, I won't let Mira suffer like this. We've saved enough money. We'll find a way out of Tuco, whatever it takes.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: All right, I'll start asking around.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Mira? When did you come in... Oh, come here and try on these clothes I just mended.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Hmm, the hem's too short. Haven't you grown taller again? My Mira just grows so fast! I'll fix this, sweetheart... Soon, we'll be able to get you beautiful new clothes.

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: It's okay, Mommy. I don't like clothes from the sellers anyway. I love the ones you made for me.

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: I'll eat less. That way I won't grow up so fast and Mommy won't have to keep fixing my clothes.
Why did Mom suddenly hug me and say sorry?
This question was too hard for my younger self. Back then, I just thought I said something wrong and made Mom cry, so I felt so bad and cried with her.

steps.speaker: DisCity Merchant
steps.content: You got all the money with you? There's plenty of hands to grease along the way. Don't count on me if you're short on cash!

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Yes, yes. Please, gentlemen, lead the way.

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Daddy, where are we going? Are we leaving our motel?

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: No, Mira, we're not leaving it. We're just... going somewhere else. There won't be any sandstorms there, and we won't have to worry about the bad people. We can open another motel...

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: My sweet girl, we're going to DisCity!

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Really? But these people look so mean, and they keep us locked up in here...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: We... we just have to wait here while they get our papers done. We'll be on our way again soon.

steps.speaker: DisCity Merchant
steps.content: Tsk, that broke loser. This isn't even worth our time. Should've known Tuco folks were all penniless. Hey, can't you find some rich marks to scam next time?

steps.speaker: Desert Bandit B
steps.content: My crap! Rich people aren't that stupid to fall for your DisCity fairy tale!

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: We already paid them, why won't they let us go... Daddy, Mommy, I'm so hungry... I'm scared. I want to go home...
Dad fought hard to keep his voice from trembling as he forced a weak smile for me.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: ...Everything will be alright, Mira. Don't be scared. We can go out soon. Everything's good...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Mira, Mira, wake up...

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Mmm... Mommy? Can we leave now?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Yes, we can leave now, sweetheart. Here's some water. Tie it to yourself. Don't drink it all at once, remember?

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Listen carefully, Mira. Once you get out of here, follow the moon and keep walking. Don't ever stop.

steps.speaker: Little Mira
steps.content: Just me alone? No, I don't want to! Why aren't you coming with me?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Because... you walk slower than us, Mira, so you need to start first. We walk much faster, and we'll catch up to you very soon.

steps.speaker: Desert Bandit
steps.content: Hey, you there! What's going on?!
The savage-looking desert bandit noticed our movement and approached us with a knife. Dad shoved me hard, pushing me through the gap he'd pried in the iron door.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: Run, Mira, run! Don't look back, just keep running!

Dad clung to the iron bars, veins bulging and eyes wild with desperation as he frantically waved me away. He roared in a hoarse voice, a sound I had never heard from his usually gentle, soft-spoken throat.

steps.speaker: Daddy
steps.content: The names Li Xianling told you would be the Realm of Yang and the Void of Yin, I imagine.
That night, the desert sky was exceptionally clear, the moon big and bright.
I ran on and on, never looking back, as if I could convince myself that Mom and Dad would indeed catch up if I didn't turn to check.
Until the pursuer's curses finally faded, until the moon set in the west and the sun rose again, until my water flask ran dry...
After fleeing for a day and a night, I finally collapsed from exhaustion on the sand, unable to get up again.
The sandstorm was spreading and the whipping wind hurt my face. Sand slipped into my eyes as I thought they would bleed. But what almost killed me was a dire thought...

It overwhelmed my exhaustion, like wildfire coursing through my body, burning through every vein until the pain became almost unbearable. I wanted nothing more than to lie down and let myself end there.
But I refused to give up like this. I was still waiting for Mom and Dad.
Huh? How come a child's lying there... Mira? Is that you, Mira?! Why are you out here alone? Where are your parents?!
Amidst adversity, this is the courage required. I'll clear a path for you!
As my consciousness slipped away, I heard the Tuco folks' cries, but still no sign of the ones who promised to catch up to me.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I was lucky. The awakening of my Sinner power pulled me back from death's door.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But by the time I woke up and begged the townsfolks to help save my parents, those desert bandits posing as DisCity merchants had vanished without a trace.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Mom and Dad... their bodies were covered in wounds, cast aside by those bastards like trash. The town's doctor said they had missed the best timing for treatment, and might... never wake up again.
As Mira tells you her story in a low voice, she picks up a photo frame from beside the hospital bed.
It's a family portrait, the colors faded with age. She gently caresses the faces in the photograph.
Though sunlight never reaches this basement, the patients' bedding still feels dry and warm. You look at Mira and feel your earlier distrust for her fading.
Your instincts tell you you can trust her through these details, this photo, and the poor middle-aged couple in it.
The deal you want to make with me, is it about your parents?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Yes. As you can see, their condition is critical. They're barely clinging to life, depending entirely on the IV and the life support machines.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But the medications and equipment maintenance cost a fortune, far more than my motel can sustain. And with Tuco constantly running with sudden desert bandit raids and disasters... I... I cannot...
So you joined the other Tuco folks in their scheme, scamming money out of travelers and even killing them when necessary.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I never wanted to do this, but... but I had no other choice!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: My parents are still here in this town, their lives in the townsfolks' hands. I had no choice but to oblige them to lie and steal...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Sometimes I dream of Mom and Dad waking up. But that would mean they'd know everything I've done, and that terrifies me. I don't know how I can ever face them...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But I'm truly grateful to have met you... You've given me hope of escaping this nightmare...
She steps closer, taking your hands in hers like clutching onto a lifeline, her eyes pleading as she looks into yours.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: I can help you escape! You can have all the Hypercubes we took from that smuggler. I know where they hid it! And if that's not enough... I'll surrender myself to the MBCC!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: But in return, I beg you, please. Once you're safe, come back here and take my parents to DisCity for treatment! This is truly... their last chance...
Mira's chest heaves with emotion, tears welling in her reddened eyes. In the brief silence that follows, you can hear her quick, anxious breathing.
Her confession sounds so heartfelt and moving that for a moment, you almost can't bring yourself to question its authenticity.
You've never been able to turn away from someone's desperate plea. Resigned, you let out a quiet sigh.
You have my word, Mira. I'll help you and take your parents to DisCity.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Really?! Oh thank goodness, Chief! I'm deeply grateful...
But rushing out recklessly isn't our best option. I've already sent an SOS to the FAC crew stationed nearby. It would be safer to wait here in the basement until they arrive.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...I see, you've thought this through, but... but there's still something concerning.
After a moment's hesitation, Mira bites her lip anxiously before speaking again.
What is it?

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: According to the original plan, I should've already gotten rid of you by now and rejoined the others... I'm worried they'll soon realize something's wrong and come look for us.
As soon as the words are out of her mouth, you hear strange noises from somewhere above you.

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Where is she? Where's Mira?! Where did she go?! Don't tell me that girl ran off with the lamb!!!

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: That can't be! We have eyes everywhere. Not even a rat can slip out of town without us knowing. Search more thoroughly! If they're not in the motel, they're somewhere in town!

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: All right, you lot guard the entrance. The rest of you, follow me into the motel!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Chief! They're already here! If we don't go now, we'll never get another chance!
Mira's grip on your hand tightens, her palm slightly damp with nervous sweat.
With your device damaged, you can't send your exact location to your team. You're not even sure if this basement door will hold until reinforcements arrive.
The chaotic footsteps and shouts draw closer. With no time left to think, you make your decision and grip Mira's hand.
...There's no other way. Mira, get us out of here!
Right outside the town of Tuco, a circular manhole cover is lifted, sending a cloud of sand into the air.
Mira emerges nimbly, tosses the bag of Hypercubes aside, then turns back to pull you out of the secret passage connecting the motel to the surface.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Here, give me your hand. Now, to get away from Tuco, all we need to do is run into the desert. Have you got anyone waiting for you out there?

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Found them! There they are! And they've got the Hypercubes!!

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: Stop them!! Don't let them get away!!!
You've just got out of the secret passage when shouts break out nearby. In the moonlight, you see multiple trails on the sand spreading rapidly toward you.
This way, run!
There's no time to waste. You grab Mira, who stands frozen in shock, and sprint in the direction where you remember your team is stationed.
In the endless expanse of nighttime WhiteSands, strong winds hurl waves of sand into your face. You can barely see where you're going, and soon Mira is pulling you along as you both stumble forward.

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: They're right ahead of us! Don't let them escape! We must get those Hypercubes back!
The same townsfolks who greeted you with warm smiles during the day are now pursuing you relentlessly like a pack of vicious, greedy hyenas.
Hasty gunfire erupts behind you as bullets barely scrape past you, sending up sprays of sand at your feet.
Bang! Bang!

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Chief, look out! ...Argh!
A violent impact shoves you aside as Mira cries out in pain. You catch her as she collapses, and find your hands stained with blood.
Hang in there! We can't give up here!
You pull Mira up and hoist her onto your shoulders, forcing your way forward with every ounce of strength you have left.
Your steps grow heavier as the shouts behind you draw closer.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: Hey... You...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You should just leave me here... I can't... drag you into this...
Don't talk. You're not dragging me into this, and I'm not breaking my promise.
You grit your teeth, hoist her onto your body, and keep running desperately.

steps.speaker: Support Squad
steps.content: ...Chief's location confirmed! I repeat, Chief's location confirmed! Hostile targets detected. Initiate defensive formation and ensure Chief's safety!

steps.speaker: Local
steps.content: ****, cops! Scatter, idiots! Get the hell back, now!

By sheer luck, your chosen escape route leads you straight into the approaching support squad. The townsfolks after you immediately turn tail, disappearing into the swirling sandstorm without a trace.

steps.speaker: Support Squad
steps.content: FAC WhiteSands operation squad reporting in. We apologize for our late arrival, Chief. Your orders, please.
With a soft clap, a trembling hand clutches yours tightly, a warm, sticky liquid trickling down your hand.

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: ...Chief... don't forget...

steps.speaker: Mira
steps.content: You've promised... You must, you must come back... for them...
With these final words, Mira falls unconscious in your arms.
Swirling sand shrouds the starry sky. In the dark, you can barely examine her wounds, but there's no ignoring the heavy scent of blood that fills your nostrils.
There's only one option to perform treatment and keep her alive. After quickly weighing the situation, you make your decision.
The Hypercubes have been retrieved. Mission accomplished. Our current priorities are to transport the Hypercubes to the disaster area and tend to the wounded.
Our targets know WhiteSands better than we do, and we can't hold out long in this sandstorm. Retreat for now and return to Tuco for the arrest later!

If what Mira told you is true, then Tuco's organized crime activities must have been ongoing and this is no single incident. Furthermore, they possess a substantial cache of weapons, making them considerably armed.
You must be extremely cautious with the pursuit of such a dangerous gang.

After making all the necessary arrangements, you immediately lead a large force across the vast barren desert, fully prepared for what's ahead. But when you finally reach this remote corner deep in the desert...

steps.speaker: Armed Squad Member A
steps.content: No way! This is not what we saw last night!
You find nothing but another stretch of barren desert.
The people, the town, the houses... Everything has vanished into thin air, like water evaporating under the sun.
...Search the area. See if they left any clues when they evacuated.

steps.speaker: Armed Squad Member B
steps.content: Chief, we found something!
All that remains of the vanished town of Tuco is an entrance leading to that basement.
...Mmph! Mmmph—!
And there, bound and abandoned at the entrance, is the wounded smuggler Mira said she had gotten rid of.
